prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: After reading all eight opening ballots I move my preferred configuration from my own first choice, IceCube (B024), to magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B033). Four members ranked it first and six placed it in their top three, and the scientific case holds up when I test it as an experimentalist would. A concrete quantitative prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) was followed years later by a decisive measurement (Jarillo-Herrero's group, 2018), and many independent groups have since reproduced the phase diagram and extended it to other moire systems. The twist angle works as a new control knob on correlated matter, which is the kind of tool that opens a field. The prediction-plus-experiment structure also gives a clean three-person prize that nearly every member who proposed names converged on (Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald, Bistritzer).
statement.case_against: The strongest reservations are attribution and maturity. Eva Andrei's earlier STM and transport evidence of flat bands in twisted layers is a credible fourth claim, and the Cao, Dean and Kim device work complicates any neat three-name split. The superconducting pairing mechanism is still unsettled, so the field is a mature platform but not a settled theory, and the discovery may be somewhat early. If the committee cannot defend excluding Andrei, the configuration fails on attribution rather than on science. I also hold B033 only third in my own opening ballot, so I am following the weight of the committee's arguments and not my own prior.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B033 first but calls the credit for the experimental discovery versus earlier flat-band spectroscopy contested, and ranks IceCube (B024) fourth, noting that a single laureate (Halzen) is a narrow reading of a collaboration of hundreds.
responses.response: I agree with the IceCube attribution objection, and it is the main reason I am not pressing my own first choice. As Chair I should not defend a one-name credit for a collaboration discovery that others also see as narrow, and a prize that omits the experiment's other leaders would be hard to justify. On B033 I share your concern about Andrei but would answer it this way. The decisive evidence is the 2018 transport observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity, and Andrei's STM work, though earlier, did not establish those phases. The committee should record that reasoning explicitly rather than ignore it.

responses.point: Eriksson values the pairing of continuum-model prediction with decisive experiment, sees credit as clear for MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and says the third seat is arguable between Bistritzer and Andrei, deferring to colleagues.
responses.response: I take the third seat to be Bistritzer. He and MacDonald wrote the paper that predicted the magic angle quantitatively, and it is a specific, falsifiable prediction that the experiment then tested. Andrei's work is real, but it is an earlier strand of evidence about flat bands and localisation in twisted layers, not the prediction or the demonstration of the correlated phases. I would still like your view as the condensed-matter specialist on whether her STM results were close enough to the prediction to count as priority. If you judge that they were, I would reconsider the third name and not simply defer.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks (B026) first, valuing the clear path from an idea (magic wavelength) to a working instrument at 1e-18, a compact two-name credit and independent confirmation across several laboratories.
responses.response: I share your instrument-builder's view of the clocks and ranked them fourth for the same reasons, and I think the attribution (Katori and Ye) is cleaner than for any other entry on the shortlist. My reservation is not scientific but one of timing. The redefinition of the second is still pending and the committee could reasonably wait for it. I would keep B026 as the first alternative if B033 is blocked on credit. I would ask you, though, whether the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes make the optical lattice clock look incremental to the wider Academy.

responses.point: Mehlig regards the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction followed by the 2018 transport discovery as the decisive pair, treats Andrei, Dean and Kim as real but secondary, and sees a theory-plus-experiment prize as fitting three names well.
responses.response: I agree with the structure, and I think it is the best argument for B033: a theoretical idea that could be shown wrong, then sharply tested. I would qualify the word 'secondary'. Calling Andrei and the device groups secondary is a judgment about priority, and the committee will have to defend it against outside criticism. I would be more comfortable if we stated plainly in the citation that the prize is for the prediction and the discovery of the correlated phases, which keeps the narrower claim and does not imply a wider one that would invite objection.

uncertainties: Whether Andrei's earlier STM and flat-band work is judged close enough to the discovery to require a place among the three laureates.
Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism of the superconductivity makes the recognition premature compared with a mature, fully understood alternative such as B009 or B026.
For B009, how to divide credit among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp and Hasan, and whether leaving out Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang can be defended.
I cannot judge condensed-matter priority claims independently and rely on the specialists on the committee for that.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B033. My collaborations are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, and I have no listed link to the moire-materials, clock or topological-insulator candidates. My only close connection on the shortlist is a shared field with IceCube (B024), my own opening first choice, with no direct collaboration listed, and I am not proposing it.
